narrative:
The model determined that you have a 28% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the status of your checking account, the loan amount you requested, and your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income. Your checking account status was the most important reason for the denial. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants and pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. The second most influential factor was the loan amount of 3,643 DM. Interestingly, this actually worked in your favor because it is only moderately above the average requested by approved applicants. Your low installment rate of 1% of disposable income was the third most important feature and also pushed the prediction toward approval, as it is well below the average seen among successful applications.

Because the negative effect from your checking account status outweighed the positive contributions from the loan size and installment rate, the overall prediction crossed the threshold for denial.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account by bringing the balance above zero and maintaining it there for several months. Once that picture looks healthier, reapply for a similar loan. This single change is likely to improve your chances substantially. (218 words)
